questions.text: The {A|ancient} Egyptians {B|developed} a calendar {C|base} on the {D|annual} flooding of the Nile.
questions.explanation: "Base" must be the past participle "based": a calendar (that was) based on the flooding. "Ancient" and "annual" are adjectives correctly placed before nouns.

questions.text: Many {A|specie} of frogs {B|are} sensitive to small {C|changes} in {D|water quality}.
questions.explanation: After "many" the noun must be plural: "species" (the same form for singular and plural). "Are" is correct because the subject is plural.

questions.text: In 1928, Alexander Fleming {A|noticed} that a mold {B|has killed} the bacteria {C|growing} in one of {D|his} culture dishes.
questions.explanation: The killing happened before Fleming noticed it in the past, so it needs the past perfect "had killed". "Growing" is a correct reduced clause ("that were growing").

questions.text: A young kangaroo {A|remains} in {B|its} mother's pouch {C|until} {D|they are} about eight months old.
questions.explanation: The pronoun refers to "a young kangaroo", an animal in the singular, so it must be "it is". "Its" in B shows the correct pronoun for the same noun.

questions.text: The success of the experiment {A|depends} largely {B|in} the {C|accuracy} {D|of} the initial measurements.
questions.explanation: The verb "depend" takes the preposition "on": "depends largely on the accuracy". "Of" in D is correct ("the accuracy of the measurements").

questions.text: {A|An} unusual feature of {B|the} octopus is that it {C|has} three hearts and {D|a} blue blood.
questions.explanation: "Blood" is an uncountable noun, so it takes no "a": "three hearts and blue blood". "The octopus" (B) is correct: "the" + singular noun can name a whole species.

questions.text: The study of volcanoes helps scientists {A|predict} eruptions, {B|protect} nearby communities, and {C|understanding} how the Earth's interior {D|works}.
questions.explanation: The three items after "helps scientists" must be parallel base verbs: predict, protect, understand. "Works" (D) is correct; it agrees with "the Earth's interior".

questions.text: The {A|economy} growth of the Roman Empire {B|depended} heavily on trade routes {C|that} stretched {D|across} the Mediterranean.
questions.explanation: Before the noun "growth" we need the adjective "economic", not the noun "economy". "Depended" (B) correctly takes "on", which follows it.

questions.text: Scientists {A|have been studying} the Antarctic ice sheet {B|since} the 1950s, and last year they {C|have recorded} {D|its} fastest rate of melting.
questions.explanation: A finished past time such as "last year" takes the simple past: "recorded", not the present perfect. "Have been studying … since the 1950s" (A) is correct because that action continues to now.

questions.text: The human skeleton {A|is made up} of more than two hundred {B|bone}, {C|which} support the body and {D|protect} its organs.
questions.explanation: After a number greater than one the noun must be plural: "two hundred bones". "Support" and "protect" are plural because "which" refers to the bones.

questions.text: A mature oak tree {A|can absorb} large amounts of carbon dioxide {B|through} {C|their} leaves {D|each} year.
questions.explanation: The pronoun refers to "a mature oak tree" (singular, not a person), so it must be "its leaves". "Can absorb" (A) is a correct modal + base verb.

questions.text: {A|Contrary of} popular belief, bats are not blind; many species {B|can see} quite well and {C|rely on} echolocation mainly {D|to hunt} in darkness.
questions.explanation: The fixed expression is "contrary to": "Contrary to popular belief". "Rely on" (C) is the correct preposition for "rely".

questions.text: The Sahara is {A|a} largest hot desert in {B|the} world, {C|covering} {D|much} of North Africa.
questions.explanation: A superlative ("largest") takes "the": "the largest hot desert". "The world" (B) is correct because there is only one.

questions.text: Archaeologists study ancient cultures by examining tools, {A|analyzing} bones, and {B|they reconstruct} {C|buildings} {D|from} ruins.
questions.explanation: All three items after "by" must be -ing forms: examining, analyzing, reconstructing. "They reconstruct" breaks the series with a full clause.

questions.text: The population of the city {A|grew} {B|rapidly} during the nineteenth century, and its streets became {C|increasingly} {D|crowd}.
questions.explanation: After the linking verb "became" we need an adjective: "crowded". "Rapidly" (B) is correct: an adverb describing the verb "grew".

questions.text: Auroras are among the most {A|beautiful} natural {B|phenomenon}, {C|appearing} as bands of colored light {D|near} the poles.
questions.explanation: "Among the most beautiful …" needs a plural noun, and the plural of "phenomenon" is "phenomena". "Appearing" (C) is a correct reduced clause describing the auroras.

questions.text: By the end of the Ice Age, many large mammals {A|had disappeared} from North America, {B|probably} because of climate change and hunting {C|by} humans who {D|arrive} only recently.
questions.explanation: The humans' arrival happened before a past point (the end of the Ice Age), so it needs the past perfect "had arrived"; the present tense "arrive" doesn't fit a past narrative. "Had disappeared" (A) is the correct past perfect for the same reason.

questions.text: The {A|discover} of oxygen in the 1770s {B|is} usually {C|credited} {D|to both} Joseph Priestley and Carl Scheele.
questions.explanation: The subject needs the noun "discovery", not the verb "discover". "Credited to both" (D) is correct ("credit something to someone").

questions.text: The Nile, {A|which} flows {B|northward}, is longer than {C|any} river in Africa and {D|provides} water to eleven countries.
questions.explanation: The Nile is itself a river in Africa, so the comparison must exclude it: "longer than any other river in Africa". Without "other" the sentence says the Nile is longer than itself. "Provides" (D) agrees with "the Nile".

questions.text: Glass is {A|made} by heating sand {B|to} a very high temperature and then {C|cooling} it {D|rapid}.
questions.explanation: "Rapid" describes how the glass is cooled, so it must be the adverb "rapidly". "Cooling" (C) is correct: it is parallel with "heating" after "by".
